\section{Supplementary Methods}

\bmhead{S1. Label processing}
ABoVE version 2\cite{Moore2025} contains \nqcAboveRaw{} thaw-depth records; after restricting to probe measurements in August--October with $0<\mathrm{ALT}<300$ cm within 45--80$^\circ$N, \nqcAboveKept{} records remained, and \nqcAboveEarly{} measurements from January--July were excluded as early-season values. CALM\cite{Streletskiy2025} contributed \nqcCalmSy{} site-years in Alaska and Canada, of which \nqcCalmNoloc{} could not be assigned to a 1 km cell, giving \nqcCalmCy{} cell-years. ALLena\cite{Veremeeva2025} contains \nqcLenaRaw{} records, of which \nqcLenaEos{} are August--September values without the measurement-limit flag; the seasonal maximum per location and year gave \nqcLenaCy{} cell-years. Of the \nqcTotalCy{} cell-years of all years, \nqcTotalCyIn{} fall in 2010--2024 and have year-specific climate input. Multiple measurements in a cell and year were averaged, and the mean day of year was kept for the accumulation of TDD.

\bmhead{S2. Climate variables}
All variables are computed from monthly ERA5-Land means for each cell and year $y$ (days per month $d_m$). TDD $=\sum_{m\in y}\max(T_m,0)\,d_m$; the cumulative TDD to the end of each month gives the observation-day value by linear interpolation in the day of year. Freezing degree-days use October $y-1$ to April $y$; the snow water equivalent is the mean of October $y-1$ to September $y$; the soil temperature is the mean of the top ERA5-Land soil layer (0--7 cm). Cells over sea in ERA5-Land use the nearest land cell within $\pm$0.2$^\circ$ and then $\pm$0.5$^\circ$. The mean climate input is the 2011--2024 mean of the yearly values (2010 is excluded because its winter variables are incomplete).

\bmhead{S3. External CALM regions}
The CALM data set\cite{Streletskiy2025} contains \nextRawSy{} site-years of 2010--2024 outside Alaska, Canada and mountain permafrost. \nextCens{} censored value (for example `$>$260') and \nextQcRm{} values with comments indicating early measurement, burning, flooding or a probe not reaching the permafrost table were removed, and sites within 100 km of the study labels were excluded. The remaining \nextcy{} cell-years in \nextcells{} cells were assigned to eight regions. Year-specific climate inputs, terrain and soil covariates and product values were computed with the same procedures as for the study regions.

\bmhead{S4. Product extraction and training data}
Yearly products were sampled at the cell centre for the observation year: Wei et al.\cite{Wei2026} from the 1 km EPSG:3995 rasters, Liu et al.\cite{Liu2024} from the 1/120$^\circ$ rasters, ESA CCI v4 and v5\cite{Westermann2024,Westermann2025} from the yearly NetCDF files, and Yi and Kimball\cite{YiKimball2019} from the Alaska NetCDF. Aalto et al.\cite{Aalto2018} provide one baseline value (2000--2014). Wei et al. were trained on 201 CALM and GTN-P sites with 2,196 annual observations of 2000--2020 and publish the site coordinates; the median distance from our label cells to the nearest site is \ndistweiAkmed{} km in Alaska, \ndistweiLemed{} km in the Lena Delta and \ndistweiCamed{} km in Canada (Supplementary Fig.~S6). Liu et al. were trained on 2,966 site-years from CALM, an earlier version of the ABoVE data (2008--2020), ABCflux and Tibetan sites. ESA CCI is a process model with remotely sensed land-surface temperature and is not trained on ALT observations. Mean product biases by latitude band (prediction minus observation) were computed on the label cell-years with a product value of the observation year.

\bmhead{S5. Product-anchored residual learning and SHAP}
In the product-anchored test, the product value $p$ of the observation year was recalibrated on the training fold as $a+bp$ (least squares), and the residual learner of the main model was trained on $y-(a+bp)$ with the same 23 features and $\lambda=0.5$. The test used the spatial-block folds of the main experiment and only the cell-years with a product value. SHAP values\cite{Lundberg2017} were computed with CatBoost's exact tree algorithm for the residual model ($y-\hat{y}_P$) and the direct model, both fitted to all labels of a region, and summarised as the mean absolute value per feature and per feature group.

\section{Supplementary Figures}
\sifig{FigS1_stefan}{Stefan relation within a season and among years. (a) Samoylov 2015: cumulative TDD, probed thaw depth (daily mean $\pm$ 1 s.d.) and the Stefan curve. (b) Thaw depth against the square root of TDD accumulated to the measurement day at Samoylov (2015) and Kurungnakh (2020), with Stefan fits. (c) Deviation of ALT from the cell mean against the deviation of $\sqrt{\mathrm{TDD}}$ at cells observed in four or more years (2010--2024). (d) Stefan coefficient $E$ by region, source coefficient and recalibrated.}{fig:s1}
\sifig{FigS2_structures}{Position of the physical information and choice of learner. Difference in spatial-block RMSE from the recalibrated Stefan model for direct ML, physics-input ML, physics pseudo-labels and the physics-residual model (a), and for the physics-residual model and direct ML with five learners (b). Labels 2010--2024; bars are 95\% block-bootstrap intervals.}{fig:s2}
\sifig{FigS3_shap}{Contribution of the input groups to the residual and direct models. Share of the mean absolute SHAP value of climate, terrain and soil variables (a) and the four largest inputs of the residual model in each region (b). Models fitted to all labels of 2010--2024.}{fig:s3}
\sifig{FigS10_label_ladder}{Label ladder with all model structures. Difference from a Stefan model recalibrated on the same labels for direct ML, physics-input ML, physics pseudo-labels and the physics-residual model (a), and the transfer ladder with all methods (b). Labels 2010--2024.}{fig:s11}
\sifig{FigS4_external}{External CALM regions (observations of \nyrsext). (a) External CALM sites, numbered by sub-region, and the label cells of the three study regions. (b) RMSE by sub-region without local labels for the physics-residual model trained on the study regions only and with its Stefan coefficient recalibrated on the other cells of the same sub-region, together with Wei et al. and Liu et al. (both trained on these sites) and ESA CCI v5 (not trained on ALT observations); each series is scored on the cell-years where it has a value, and numbers in brackets are cell-years. (c) RMSE of the physics-residual model with no and with five local labels and of ESA CCI v5 on the cell-years with values of all three products, for the six sub-regions with at least 30 such cell-years; Kamchatka (16 cell-years) enters only the pooled value of Fig.~4c of the main text.}{fig:s5}
\sifig{FigS5_training_sites}{Distance to product training sites and differences between product maps and our map. (a) Training sites of Wei et al. and the label cells of the three regions (2010--2024). (b) Cumulative share of label cells against the distance to the nearest training site of Wei et al.; the dashed line marks 25 km. (c) Mean difference between each product and our Alaska map of 2014 by latitude band, for cells at or below and above 600 m elevation (every tenth 1 km cell).}{fig:s10}
\sifig{FigS6_product_anchor}{Product-anchored and Stefan-anchored residual learning. RMSE on the label cell-years with a value of Wei et al. for the observation year (Alaska and Canada 2010--2024, Lena Delta 2013--2021; $n$ is the number of cell-years) under spatial-block cross-validation: the product as published, the product linearly recalibrated on the training folds (equation (8) of the main text), the recalibrated product with a residual learner, the recalibrated Stefan model and the physics-residual model.}{fig:s4}
\sifig{FigS7_map_detail}{Detail of the 1 km maps and area of applicability. (a, b) Mean ALT of 2011--2024 in Alaska in two 50 km windows near Toolik (North Slope) and Fairbanks (Interior), drawn as 1 km cells over hillshade. (c) Area of applicability of the Alaska map with the two windows. (d) ALT of the Lena Delta in 2016. (e) Samoylov and Kurungnakh window.}{fig:s9}
\sifig{FigS8_correction_maps}{Residual correction of the Stefan model. Physics-residual minus recalibrated Stefan prediction per 1 km cell for (a) the mean of the Alaska yearly maps of 2011--2024 and (b) the Lena Delta in 2016; negative values indicate that the residual learner lowers the Stefan estimate. The 1 km values are interpolated to 250 m for display.}{fig:s7}
\sifig{FigS9_site_series}{Yearly series at long-record cells.
